description: Leibniz Encyclopedia: seed knowledge base of theorems (informal + Lean 4) used by the StubBackend and the conceptual-alignment gate. Lean proofs use Lean 4 core (no Mathlib) so they compile in the bundled leibniz/lean project. Deeper entries are stated but intentionally NOT certified in core to illustrate hard-conjecture discovery.

entries.name: two_plus_two
entries.informal: The sum of two and two equals four.
entries.lean_statement: theorem two_plus_two : 2 + 2 = 4
entries.rationale: The simplest possible check that formal numerals reduce correctly under definitional equality.

entries.name: three_times_three
entries.informal: Three multiplied by three equals nine.
entries.lean_statement: theorem three_times_three : 3 * 3 = 9
entries.rationale: Foundational multiplicative identity; verifies kernel reduction for Nat literals.

entries.name: ten_minus_four
entries.informal: Ten minus four equals six.
entries.lean_statement: theorem ten_minus_four : 10 - 4 = 6
entries.rationale: Checks truncating subtraction on natural-number literals.

entries.name: add_zero_left
entries.informal: For every natural number n, n + 0 = n.
entries.lean_statement: theorem add_zero_left (n : Nat) : n + 0 = n
entries.rationale: The left identity law for addition; a universal (quantified) statement rather than a closed numeric fact.

entries.name: add_comm_nat
entries.informal: Addition of natural numbers is commutative: a + b = b + a.
entries.lean_statement: theorem add_comm_nat (a b : Nat) : a + b = b + a
entries.rationale: Commutativity is a structural property of addition; exercising core rewrite lemmas.

entries.name: mul_one_right
entries.informal: For every natural number n, n * 1 = n.
entries.lean_statement: theorem mul_one_right (n : Nat) : n * 1 = n
entries.rationale: Multiplicative right identity; reduces definitionally via the base equation of Nat.mul.

entries.name: even_square_is_even
entries.informal: The square of an even number is divisible by four.
entries.lean_statement: theorem even_square_is_even (n : Nat) : (2 * n) ^ 2 = 4 * (n ^ 2)
entries.rationale: A first bridge between arithmetic and multiplicative number theory: parity is preserved under squaring.

entries.name: infinitude_of_primes
entries.informal: There are infinitely many prime numbers.
entries.lean_statement: theorem infinitude_of_primes : ∀ n, ∃ p, p > n ∧ Nat.Prime p
entries.rationale: Euclid's classical theorem. Stated here as a hard discovery target; a full Lean proof requires Nat.Prime machinery (Mathlib).

entries.name: fermat_little
entries.informal: Fermat's little theorem: if p is prime and p does not divide a, then p divides a^(p-1) - 1.
entries.lean_statement: theorem fermat_little (p : Nat) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (a : Nat) (ha : ¬ p ∣ a) : p ∣ a ^ (p - 1) - 1
entries.rationale: A pillar of elementary number theory; formalization requires substantial Mathlib group/ring machinery.

entries.name: bertrand_postulate
entries.informal: Bertrand's postulate: for every n > 1 there is a prime strictly between n and 2n.
entries.lean_statement: theorem bertrand_postulate : ∀ n > 1, ∃ p, n < p ∧ p < 2 * n ∧ Nat.Prime p
entries.rationale: A non-trivial result on prime distribution; deep formalization target.

entries.name: set_union_self
entries.informal: The union of any set with itself equals itself.
entries.lean_statement: theorem set_union_self (α : Type) (s : Set α) : s ∪ s = s
entries.rationale: Idempotence of union; a basic law of set algebra.

entries.name: add_comm_vec
entries.informal: Vector addition is commutative: for all vectors v, w in ℝⁿ, v + w = w + v.
entries.lean_statement: theorem add_comm_vec (v w : Fin n → ℝ) : v + w = w + v
entries.lean_proof: by ext i; exact add_comm (v i) (w i)
entries.rationale: Pointwise addition of functions is commutative because ℝ addition is commutative.

entries.name: add_assoc_vec
entries.informal: Vector addition is associative: for all vectors u, v, w in ℝⁿ, (u + v) + w = u + (v + w).
entries.lean_statement: theorem add_assoc_vec (u v w : Fin n → ℝ) : (u + v) + w = u + (v + w)
entries.lean_proof: by ext i; exact add_assoc (u i) (v i) (w i)
entries.rationale: Pointwise addition inherits associativity from ℝ.

entries.name: zero_add_vec
entries.informal: The zero vector is a left identity: for every vector v in ℝⁿ, 0 + v = v.
entries.lean_statement: theorem zero_add_vec (v : Fin n → ℝ) : 0 + v = v
entries.rationale: The zero function plus any function is that function.

entries.name: add_neg_vec
entries.informal: Every vector has an additive inverse: v + (-v) = 0 for every v in ℝⁿ.
entries.lean_statement: theorem add_neg_vec (v : Fin n → ℝ) : v + (-v) = 0
entries.rationale: A vector added to its pointwise negation yields the zero vector.

entries.name: smul_add_vec
entries.informal: Scalar multiplication distributes over vector addition: c · (v + w) = c·v + c·w.
entries.lean_statement: theorem smul_add_vec (c : ℝ) (v w : Fin n → ℝ) : c • (v + w) = c • v + c • w
entries.lean_proof: by ext i; exact mul_add c (v i) (w i)
entries.rationale: Scalars distribute over pointwise addition because ℝ multiplication distributes over addition.

entries.name: add_smul_vec
entries.informal: Scalar multiplication distributes over scalar addition: (c + d)·v = c·v + d·v.
entries.lean_statement: theorem add_smul_vec (c d : ℝ) (v : Fin n → ℝ) : (c + d) • v = c • v + d • v
entries.lean_proof: by ext i; exact add_mul c d (v i)
entries.rationale: ℝ field addition distributes over multiplication; lifts pointwise to vectors.

entries.name: smul_assoc_vec
entries.informal: Scalar multiplication is associative: c · (d · v) = (c·d) · v.
entries.lean_statement: theorem smul_assoc_vec (c d : ℝ) (v : Fin n → ℝ) : c • (d • v) = (c * d) • v
entries.rationale: ℝ multiplication is associative; lifts pointwise to scalar multiplication of vectors.

entries.name: one_smul_vec
entries.informal: The scalar 1 is the identity for scalar multiplication: 1·v = v.
entries.lean_statement: theorem one_smul_vec (v : Fin n → ℝ) : (1 : ℝ) • v = v
entries.rationale: Multiplying each component by 1 leaves it unchanged — the vector-space unity law.

entries.name: linear_combination_zero
entries.informal: If vectors v and w satisfy a·v + b·w = 0 with a, b nonzero for all components, then v and w are linearly dependent.
entries.lean_statement: theorem linear_combination_zero (a b : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (v w : Fin 2 → ℝ) (h : a • v + b • w = 0) : ∃ c : ℝ, w = c • v
entries.rationale: A core concept of linear algebra — expressed as a hard discovery target requiring existential reasoning over ℝⁿ components.

entries.name: determinant_2x2
entries.informal: The determinant of a 2×2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]] is ad − bc. A matrix is invertible iff its determinant is nonzero.
entries.lean_statement: -- determinant_2x2 (a b c d : ℝ) : det [[a,b],[c,d]] = a*d - b*c
entries.rationale: Determinants are the gateway to eigenvalues and invertibility; a hard formalization target needing matrix representations.

entries.name: eigenvalue_id
entries.informal: Every nonzero vector is an eigenvector of the identity transformation with eigenvalue 1.
entries.lean_statement: theorem eigenvalue_id (v : Fin n → ℝ) (hv : v ≠ 0) : (λ x : Fin n → ℝ => x) v = (1 : ℝ) • v
entries.rationale: The simplest spectral theorem check — the identity acts as scalar 1 on every vector.

entries.name: basis_standard_rn
entries.informal: Any vector in ℝⁿ can be expressed uniquely as a linear combination of the standard basis vectors e₁, …, eₙ.
entries.lean_statement: -- Every v: Fin n → ℝ can be written as Σ_i (v i) · e_i where e_i j = 1 if i=j else 0.
entries.rationale: The standard basis is the foundational spanning set; formalizing full unique representation is a hard theorem.

entries.name: rh_critical_line
entries.informal: (Domain example) The first few non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie on the critical line Re(s)=1/2.
entries.lean_statement: -- Stated numerically, not formally: zeros at gamma = 14.1347, 21.0220, 25.0109, ...
entries.rationale: Connects the engine to this repository's Riemann-Hypothesis toolkit; a numerical, not formal, conjecture.

entries.name: subspace_criterion
entries.informal: A nonempty subset W of a vector space V is a subspace iff it is closed under addition and scalar multiplication.
entries.lean_statement: theorem subspace_criterion (K V : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (W : Set V) (hW : W.Nonempty) : Subspace K V ↔ ∀ (a b : K) (x y ∈ W), a • x + b • y ∈ W
entries.rationale: The fundamental subspace test. Requires Mathlib's Module/Submodule machinery.

entries.name: span_is_subspace
entries.informal: The span of any subset of a vector space is a subspace.
entries.lean_statement: theorem span_is_subspace (K V : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (S : Set V) : Subspace K V
entries.rationale: The span is the smallest subspace containing a set — a core construction.

entries.name: basis_dim_welldefined
entries.informal: Any two bases of a finite-dimensional vector space have the same cardinality (the dimension is well-defined).
entries.lean_statement: theorem basis_dim_welldefined (K V : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] {ι ι' : Type*} (b : Basis ι K V) (b' : Basis ι' K V) [Fintype ι] [Fintype ι'] : Fintype.card ι = Fintype.card ι'
entries.rationale: Invariance of dimension — the theorem that makes 'dimension' meaningful.

entries.name: every_vs_has_basis
entries.informal: Every finitely-generated vector space has a finite basis.
entries.lean_statement: theorem every_vs_has_basis (K V : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] : ∃ (n : ℕ), Nonempty (Basis (Fin n) K V)
entries.rationale: Existence of bases for finite-dimensional spaces.

entries.name: rank_nullity
entries.informal: Rank-Nullity theorem: for a linear map f : V → W between finite-dimensional spaces, dim(range f) + dim(kernel f) = dim V.
entries.lean_statement: theorem rank_nullity (K V W : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] [FiniteDimensional K V] [FiniteDimensional K W] (f : V →ₗ[K] W) : finrank K (LinearMap.range f) + finrank K (LinearMap.ker f) = finrank K V
entries.rationale: The fundamental theorem of linear maps — relates image and kernel dimensions.

entries.name: injective_iff_ker_bot
entries.informal: A linear map is injective if and only if its kernel is trivial (equals {0}).
entries.lean_statement: theorem injective_iff_ker_bot (K V W : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] (f : V →ₗ[K] W) : Function.Injective f ↔ LinearMap.ker f = ⊥
entries.rationale: Characterises injective linear maps via their kernel — central to isomorphisms.

entries.name: linear_map_preserves_combination
entries.informal: A linear map preserves linear combinations: f(a·v + b·w) = a·f(v) + b·f(w).
entries.lean_statement: theorem linear_map_preserves_combination (K V W : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] (f : V →ₗ[K] W) (a b : K) (v w : V) : f (a • v + b • w) = a • f v + b • f w
entries.rationale: The defining property of linearity, stated in full generality.

entries.name: image_of_subspace_is_subspace
entries.informal: The image of a subspace under a linear map is a subspace of the codomain.
entries.lean_statement: theorem image_of_subspace_is_subspace (K V W : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module K W] (f : V →ₗ[K] W) (S : Submodule K V) : ∃ T : Submodule K W, T = Submodule.map f S
entries.rationale: Linear maps send subspaces to subspaces.

entries.name: det_mul
entries.informal: The determinant is multiplicative: det(A·B) = det(A)·det(B) for n×n matrices.
entries.lean_statement: theorem det_mul (K : Type*) [Field K] (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) : det (A * B) = det A * det B
entries.rationale: Determinant is a multiplicative homomorphism on the matrix ring.

entries.name: det_transpose
entries.informal: A matrix and its transpose have the same determinant: det(Aᵀ) = det(A).
entries.lean_statement: theorem det_transpose (K : Type*) [Field K] (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) : det Aᵀ = det A
entries.rationale: Transpose-invariance of the determinant.

entries.name: invertible_iff_det_ne_zero
entries.informal: A square matrix over a field is invertible if and only if its determinant is nonzero.
entries.lean_statement: theorem invertible_iff_det_ne_zero (K : Type*) [Field K] (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) : Invertible A ↔ det A ≠ 0
entries.rationale: The bridge between invertibility and the determinant — underpins solving linear systems.

entries.name: matrix_rank_col_eq_row
entries.informal: The column rank and row rank of a matrix are equal.
entries.lean_statement: theorem matrix_rank_col_eq_row (K : Type*) [Field K] (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) K) : finrank K (Submodule.span K (Matrix.range A)) = finrank K (Submodule.span K (Set.range (fun i => Aᵀ i)))
entries.rationale: Row rank equals column rank — a foundational and non-obvious fact.

entries.name: eigenvector_nonzero
entries.informal: Every eigenvector is, by definition, a nonzero vector v with A·v = λ·v for some scalar λ.
entries.lean_statement: theorem eigenvector_nonzero (K V : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (f : End K V) (v : V) (hv : f.IsEigenvector v) : v ≠ 0
entries.rationale: The nonzero requirement on eigenvectors guarantees eigenvalue uniqueness.

entries.name: real_symmetric_real_eigenvalues
entries.informal: Every eigenvalue of a real symmetric matrix is real.
entries.lean_statement: theorem real_symmetric_real_eigenvalues (n : Type*) (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (hA : A.IsSymm) : ∀ (λ : ℂ), A.HasEigenvalue λ → λ ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℝ → ℂ)
entries.rationale: The spectral theorem's first half — symmetry forces real spectrum.

entries.name: cayley_hamilton
entries.informal: Cayley-Hamilton theorem: every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation, p_A(A) = 0.
entries.lean_statement: theorem cayley_hamilton (K : Type*) [Field K] (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) : A.eval (charpoly A) = 0
entries.rationale: A matrix annihilated by its characteristic polynomial — a deep algebraic fact.

entries.name: orthogonal_vectors_independent
entries.informal: A set of nonzero mutually-orthogonal vectors is linearly independent.
entries.lean_statement: theorem orthogonal_vectors_independent {V : Type*} [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] {s : Set V} (h : ∀ (x y ∈ s), x ≠ y → ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ = 0) (hnz : ∀ x ∈ s, x ≠ 0) : LinearIndependent ℝ ((↑) : s → V)
entries.rationale: Orthogonality implies independence — the basis for Gram-Schmidt.

entries.name: sq_nonneg
entries.informal: The square of any real number is nonnegative (x^2 >= 0).
entries.lean_statement: theorem sq_nonneg (x : Real) : 0 <= x ^ 2
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.2 'Basics' - the first analytic inequality.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.2 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: abs_nonneg
entries.informal: The absolute value of a real number is nonnegative.
entries.lean_statement: theorem abs_nonneg (x : Real) : 0 <= |x|
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.2 - basic absolute-value facts underpinning limits.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.2 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: irrational_sqrt_two
entries.informal: The square root of 2 is irrational.
entries.lean_statement: theorem irrational_sqrt_two : Irrational (Real.sqrt 2)
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.5 'Elementary Number Theory' - the classic irrationality proof.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.5 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: exists_infinite_primes
entries.informal: There are infinitely many primes (Euclid).
entries.lean_statement: theorem exists_infinite_primes : forall n, exists p > n, Nat.Prime p
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.5 - Euclid's theorem with Mathlib's Nat.Prime.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.5 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: schroder_bernstein
entries.informal: Schroder-Bernstein: injections X->Y and Y->X give a bijection X->Y.
entries.lean_statement: theorem schroder_bernstein {X Y : Type*} (f : X -> Y) (g : Y -> X) (hf : Function.Injective f) (hg : Function.Injective g) : exists h : X -> Y, Function.Bijective h
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.4 'Sets and Functions' - culminating proof exercise.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.4 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: finset_card_powerset
entries.informal: A finite set with n elements has 2^n subsets.
entries.lean_statement: theorem finset_card_powerset {a : Type*} [Fintype a] : Fintype.card (Set a) = 2 ^ Fintype.card a
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.6 'Discrete Mathematics' - counting subsets.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.6 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: group_inv_inv
entries.informal: In a group, (a^-1)^-1 = a.
entries.lean_statement: theorem group_inv_inv {G : Type*} [Group G] (a : G) : (a^-1)^-1 = a
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.9 'Groups and Rings' - the first structural lemma.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.9 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: group_mul_left_inv
entries.informal: In a group, a^-1 * a = 1.
entries.lean_statement: theorem group_mul_left_inv {G : Type*} [Group G] (a : G) : a^-1 * a = 1
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.9 - the defining group axiom as a lemma.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.9 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: mul_left_cancel_group
entries.informal: In a group, a * b = a * c implies b = c.
entries.lean_statement: theorem mul_left_cancel_group {G : Type*} [Group G] {a b c : G} (h : a * b = a * c) : b = c
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.9 - left cancellation in groups.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.9 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: submodule_span_union
entries.informal: The span of a union is the sum of the spans.
entries.lean_statement: theorem submodule_span_union {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (S T : Set V) : span K (S union T) = span K S ⊔ span K T
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.10 'Linear Algebra' - span and the submodule lattice.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.10 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: matrix_trace_additive
entries.informal: The trace is additive: tr(A + B) = tr A + tr B.
entries.lean_statement: theorem matrix_trace_additive (K : Type*) [Field K] (A B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) : (A + B).trace = A.trace + B.trace
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.10 - trace as a linear functional.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.10 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: continuous_at_id
entries.informal: The identity map is continuous at every point.
entries.lean_statement: theorem continuous_at_id {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] (x : X) : ContinuousAt (fun y : X => y) x
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.11 'Topology' - the first continuity fact.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.11 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: tendsto_const
entries.informal: A constant function tends to its value.
entries.lean_statement: theorem tendsto_const {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace Y] (c : Y) (x : X) : Filter.Tendsto (fun _ : X => c) (Filter.principal {x}) (Filter.principal {c})
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.11 - the first Tendsto lemma.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.11 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: deriv_const
entries.informal: The derivative of a constant is zero.
entries.lean_statement: theorem deriv_const (c : Real) : deriv (fun _ : Real => c) = 0
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.12 'Differential Calculus' - the first derivative fact.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.12 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: deriv_id
entries.informal: The derivative of the identity is 1.
entries.lean_statement: theorem deriv_id : deriv (fun x : Real => x) = 1
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.12 - the identity has derivative 1.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.12 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: measure_union_disjoint
entries.informal: The measure of a disjoint union is the sum of the measures.
entries.lean_statement: theorem measure_union_disjoint {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] (m : Measure X) {s t : Set X} (hs : MeasurableSet s) (ht : MeasurableSet t) (hd : Disjoint s t) : m (s union t) = m s + m t
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.13 'Integration and Measure Theory' - finite additivity.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.13 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)

entries.name: integrable_const
entries.informal: A constant function is integrable on a finite-measure space.
entries.lean_statement: theorem integrable_const {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] (m : Measure X) [IsFiniteMeasure m] (c : Real) : Integrable (fun _ : X => c) m
entries.rationale: MiL Ch.13 - constant functions are integrable.
entries.source: Mathematics in Lean, Ch.13 (Avigad-Massot, CC BY 4.0)
